data.name: Narinder
data.gender_notes: Narinder is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nari (Lady) + Indra (Lord of the Heavens) -> The ruler of the people, the one who protects the masses. The name Narinder carries the meaning “Lord of the People” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Narinder usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes leadership, protection, and divine intervention.
data.etymology: Narinder belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the People.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Narinder total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Narinder represents a figure of great leadership and protection. Indra, the god of rain and thunder, has played a significant role in history as the major deity in the ancient Hindu civilization. Being named Narinder is a clear indication of someone who is expected to lead and protect their community, much like the god Indra protects his people in the heavens.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Narinder highlights the aspect of lordship, power, and protection. Indra is known as the "god of gods", proving that the person bearing this name is considered divine in their community. The name also emphasizes the importance of leadership and looking out for the well-being of others. Ultimately, the name Narinder serves as a reminder of one's spiritual duty to serve, protect, and lead their community.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Narinder: Radiant as the Lord Narayana. Embodiment of divine light, compassion, and wisdom.
